person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper, we propose Political Delegitimization Discourse (PDD) as a distinct analytical category and introduce a computational pipeline for its large-scale detection and characterization.

span.label: political delegitimization discourse
span.quote: Political Delegitimization Discourse (PDD) is defined as discourse that seeks to undermine the legitimacy of political identities through attacks against their symbolic aspects, rather than criticizing specific policies or actions.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We introduce a twostage classification pipeline, and benchmark finetuned encoder models and decoder LLMs.

span.label: The study's scope and transferability are limited.
span.quote: A key limitation of our study concerns its scope and transferability.

span.label: Findings from the Hebrew-language, Israeli case may not generalize to other languages or political systems.
span.quote: While our Hebrew-language corpus and Israeli political focus enable an indepth case study, the findings may not directly generalize to other linguistic or institutional and political contexts.

span.label: The social media analysis covers only Facebook posts from 2018-2021, excluding other platforms and later periods.
span.quote: Likewise, our social-media analysis is limited to Facebook posts from 2018-2021, leaving unexamined discourse on other platforms and in more recent periods.

span.label: Porting the approach to other languages and political contexts is expected to be difficult because delegitimization is shaped by local dynamics.
span.quote: The transfer of our approach to other languages and political contexts may pose several challenges.

span.label: The category is defined by excluding policy criticism, a line a coder must draw in each sentence.
span.quote: sentence is considered positive for PDD if it targets a political actor, group, or institution and conveys a hostile characterization not grounded in policy critique but in symbol-based delegitimization

span.label: Reliability was established on a 170-sentence sample by coders who include the study's lead author.
span.quote: Delegitimization was annotated as a binary category (T/F) by three human annotators, including the lead author and two graduate students. A sample of 170 sentences was used for inter-coder reliability, showing a high average correlation of 0.91 between the annotators and an average Cohen’s Kappa of 0.82, indicating substantial agreement

span.label: Only a sixth of the labelled corpus carries the finer annotations the characterisation rests on.
span.quote: We curate and manually annotate a novel Hebrew-language corpus of 10,410 sentences drawn from parliamentary speeches (1993- 2023), Facebook posts, and leading news outlets (2018-2021), of which 1,812 instances (17.4%) exhibit PDD and 642 carry additional annotations for intensity, incivility, target type, and affective framing

span.label: The category is proposed by this paper rather than inherited from the literature.
span.quote: In this paper, we propose Political Delegitimization Discourse (PDD) as a distinct analytical category and introduce a computational pipeline for its large-scale detection and characterization

span.label: PDD - A STIPULATED CATEGORY WHOSE BOUNDARY IS SYMBOL VERSUS POLICY: hostility toward a political actor counts only when it is not grounded in policy critique, so the same anger about the same target falls inside or outside the category depending on what the coder judges it to be aimed at
span.quote: sentence is considered positive for PDD if it targets a political actor, group, or institution and conveys a hostile characterization not grounded in policy critique but in symbol-based delegitimization

span.label: the boundary, SHOWN RATHER THAN STATED: the paper prints a sentence calling a budget an example of negligence and promiscuous conduct endangering the economy and society, and records that it is NOT annotated as PDD - a published negative case, which is rarer in this corpus than a definition
span.quote: For example, the sentence “This [budget] is an example of negligence and promiscuous conduct, endangering both the economy and society in Israel.” is not annotated as PDD

span.label: the conceptual definition BEHIND the annotation scheme: discourse aimed at discrediting political groups or actors by attacking their symbolic and affective dimensions - the scheme is built on that phrase, and every count in the paper inherits it
span.quote: We developed an annotation scheme grounded in a conceptual definition of PDD as discourse aimed at discrediting political groups or actors by attacking their symbolic and affective dimensions

span.label: builds-on → Rivlin-Angert (2025), on delegitimization of political identities
span.quote: The objective of PDD is to establish political dominance and suppress alternative narratives by narrowing the boundaries of acceptable discourse and excluding specific ideas and ideologies from being considered legitimate (Rivlin-Angert, 2025).

span.label: builds-on → Mor-Lan et al. (2024), IsraParlTweet dataset of Knesset speeches
span.quote: We utilize the Isra- ParlTweet dataset (Mor-Lan et al., 2024), a full archive of Knesset floor speeches from 1992-2023.

span.label: builds-on → Monroe et al. (2008), weighted log odds method
span.quote: Using the weighted log odds method proposed by Monroe et al. (2008), we identify the PDD target tokens most strongly associated with each political bloc.

span.label: extends → existing NLP tasks: toxicity detection, stance detection, targeted sentiment analysis
span.quote: Our work extends beyond existing NLP tasks such as toxicity detection, stance detection, and targeted sentiment analysis.

span.label: PDD —same-as→ Political Delegitimization Discourse
span.quote: In this paper, we propose Political Delegitimization Discourse (PDD) as a distinct analytical category

span.label: PDD —distinct-from→ policy critique
span.quote: sentence is considered positive for PDD if it targets a political actor, group, or institution and conveys a hostile characterization not grounded in policy critique but in symbol-based delegitimization

span.label: Earlier computational work on hostile political speech classified abuse directed at politicians rather than attacks on legitimacy itself.
span.quote: Early approaches used supervised classifiers to identify abusive language directed at politicians
